subject: request for a Jupyter notebook that showcases / demonstrates Stan (using Python or Julia) in economics

messages.author: da33143a8db60ce8
messages.subject: request for a Jupyter notebook that showcases / demonstrates Stan (using Python or Julia) in economics
parts:
Hi all. See below. Matthew McKay is an economist who is part of a group developing open-source quantitative economics tools. We suggested he use Stan for his Bayesian and maximum likelihood needs (since Stan is so general, it can fit all sorts of models such as measurement error models, arbitrary correlation specifications, etc., that can be difficult to fit in other software) and here is how he replied:

> On Jan 20, 2016, at 9:04 PM, Matthew McKay <matthe...@nyu.edu> wrote:
>
> As part of QuantEcon we also host a Jupyter notebook gallery:
> http://quantecon.org/notebooks.html to help demonstrate and showcase
> tools that are available for Quantitative Economics (Research and
> Teaching). If there was a Jupyter notebook that showcases /
> demonstrates Stan (python or julia) in economics we would be happy to
> post them.

If anyone out there in Stan user-land is interested in doing this, that would be great!

See you
A

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] request for a Jupyter notebook that showcases / demonstrates Stan (using Python or Julia) in economics
parts:
All their examples are in Python, but Jupyter can be
done in R or Julia, too.

They already have a PyMC example:

http://nbviewer.jupyter.org/github/QuantEcon/QuantEcon.notebooks/blob/master/ar1_pymc.ipynb

Reading econometrics is like reading a foreign language.

They want contributions in the form of GitHub pull requests.
We were just talking about how high that hurdle would be for
users yesterday. Any thoughts?

Andrew --- we should get you set up so you can try
one yourself! But then it looks like they want contributions
in the form of GitHub pull requests --- we were just
talking about asking users to do that and I figured it'd
be too hard.

- Bob

Aki
